page.text:
The *kernel* (or null space) $\ker(T) = \{v \in V : T(v) = 0\}$ consists
of all vectors annihilated by $T$. The kernel is a subspace of $V$, and
measures the failure of $T$ to be injective:
$T(u) = T(v) \iff u - v \in \ker(T)$. Consequently, $T$ is injective if
and only if $\ker(T) = \{0\}$. For any $w \in \operatorname{im}(T)$, the
fiber $T^{-1}(w)$ is an affine subspace of the form $v_0 + \ker(T)$.
